title: resolve-spawn.py rewrites spawns.json with indent=2/ensure_ascii=True, churning the whole file
detail: The PostToolUse hook appends spawn rows but re-serializes the whole file at indent=2 with ASCII escapes, while the repo's ledgers are indent=1 with literal UTF-8. Every session's spawns.json therefore shows ~1000 changed lines instead of ~10, and each wrapup has to re-normalize by hand before committing. Observed 2026-07-29 session 35: `git diff --stat flywheel/state/spawns.json` = 1057 insertions / 1017 deletions for 5 appended rows. Fix: make flywheel/resolve-spawn.py dump with indent=1, ensure_ascii=False. FIXED on branch `flywheel/improve-spawn-ledger-indent` (commit 8425d40, one commit off main), verifier VERIFIED 2026-07-29. Human approved the merge; merged --no-ff into main. Post-merge gates green.

title: compact.py writes ledgers at indent=2, which would revert i28's spawns.json normalization
detail: flywheel/compact.py:20 writes state ledgers with `indent=2` (ensure_ascii=False). It is the second writer of the same files that i28 fixed in flywheel/resolve-spawn.py, so the next compaction run would re-churn spawns.json indentation and also churn activity.json (indent=1 today). This is live, not theoretical: flywheel/check.sh already prints `⚠ state/spawns.json: 109 entries (>100) — compaction due (python3 flywheel/compact.py)` and flywheel/MAINTENANCE.md:39-41 schedules that compaction for an improve pass. Found while planning i28; plan-auditor confirmed that keeping it OUT of i28's commit is correct (separate file, separate revert unit) but required an explicit stop-instruction, recorded at docs/flywheel/plans/improve-i26-i27-i28.md §0.5: do NOT run compaction until this is fixed. Fix: compact.py to indent=1, own branch, then run compaction. FIXED on branch `flywheel/improve-compact-ledger-indent` (commit 0fe6afa, one commit off main 726bbc9): source + distribution mirror both `indent=1, ensure_ascii=False`. Fresh verifier VERIFIED 2026-07-29 (7/7 criteria, incl. an A7 probe confirming no third indent=2 writer of flywheel/state). Human approved d34; merged --no-ff into main as 778f856, post-merge gates green. The blocked compaction then ran: activity.json 37->31, spawns.json 110->31 entries, 21 insertions / 860 deletions with no indentation churn.

title: Spawn ledger records outcome "ok" unconditionally, and for background spawns writes it before the agent finishes
detail: flywheel/resolve-spawn.py:547 and :572 hardcode `"outcome": "ok"`, so no spawn row can ever read retried/escalated/failed — yet IMPROVE.md:23 tells the improve pass to gather `state/spawns.json` rows with outcome `retried|escalated|failed`, which by construction returns nothing. Observed 2026-07-29 while fixing i29: the claude-code PostToolUse hook (.claude/settings.json, matcher `Agent`) fires when the Agent tool CALL returns, and a background spawn returns at launch, so the verifier row `{ts 2026-07-29T16:59, agent verifier, task "Verify i29 compact indent fix", outcome "ok"}` was already in the ledger while that verifier was still running — the verifier itself flagged it as a possibly fabricated success entry. Provenance is legitimate (framework hook, notes `auto-logged`), but the row asserts an outcome that did not exist yet. Fix candidates: drop the outcome field from auto-logged rows or set it to `pending`/`unknown` and have wrapup fill the real outcome, or move background-spawn logging to a completion-time signal. Own branch; do not bundle. FIXED 2026-07-29 on flywheel/improve-i30-spawn-outcome (08ae05d, plan 81874da), verifier VERIFIED 8/8; awaiting the d36 merge decision — closes on merge. Residual, stated by the verifier: nothing mechanically forces a pending row to a terminal value (check.sh only warns), so that step rests on the wrapup skill body being obeyed.

title: Lifecycle suite aborts on the first runner, so a node-only regression can hide behind a python3 failure
detail: tests/test_adapter_lifecycle.sh runs each exercise for runner=python3 then runner=node under `set -euo pipefail`, so the first python3 failure aborts the script before any node case executes. Observed 2026-07-29 by the i19 verifier: reverting installer/lifecycle/common.sh failed at `runner=python3, value=''` and the node case was never reached; only the verifier's separate harness proved the node path was independently broken. Consequence: for any defect present in both wire_block heredocs, the suite reports one runner's status and stays silent on the other — exactly the divergence the dual-heredoc design most needs covered. Fix candidates: collect failures per runner and report at the end instead of aborting, or run the two runner matrices as separate top-level invocations.
